verdict.rationale: Browserbase is a browser and web-data platform for agents, so adaptive crawling is a fair axis to ask about. The evidence covers search, URL fetch, concurrent sessions, and goal-driven agents. None of it documents a crawler that measures information sufficiency and stops automatically once it has enough to answer the query. Goal-described agents and pausing runs (pauseWhen, which waits for human input) are adjacent features, not this capability.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can rely on adaptive crawling that automatically stops once enough information has been gathered to answer my query
